body.estimand_functional: \(\theta=H/B-1=\sum_{(g,t)\in\mathcal D}(w^0_{gt}/B)(v_{gt}-1)\), with exact honest inference defined by \(D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)\) and \(D_{\mathrm{rand}}(\kappa)\)

sampling_model.design: Condition on observed \(s\in\mathcal S_T\) and on calibrated, known \(\kappa>0\); require honesty uniformly over the entire observed-share simplex.
sampling_model.units: The observations are the fixed collection of cohort--time totals \(X_{gt}\), not an individual-level sample or a finite-population randomization.
sampling_model.treatment: Cohort \(g\) is untreated for \(t<g\) and treated for \(t\ge g\); the never-treated cohort is indexed by \(\infty\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cohort share is at least \(1/(2T)\). The exposure, time-effect, and treated-multiplier boxes are separately maintained restrictions on the aggregate-Poisson experiment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite-count inference profiles \(A,b,v\) exactly under the product-Poisson likelihood. The high-intensity bridge estimates normalized row and time effects from untreated cells and treated totals. Estimating or jointly calibrating an unknown intensity is not covered.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The estimator uses the ratio of average observed and counterfactual outcomes.
Pooled canonical-link quasi-likelihood and imputation produce identical cohort-time estimates under the stated nonlinear parallel-trends model.
Fixed-effect averages are consistent and asymptotically normal with the cross section growing and fixed \(T\).
Minimax expected-measure confidence sets are characterized using Bayes--minimax duality.
Theorem 6 controls off-support maximum risk while the finite-prior Monte Carlo procedure converges to its game value.
The scalar Poisson interval cannot be shortened without lowering infimal coverage below its nominal level.
Auxiliary-uniform randomization splits binomial atoms and yields exact equi-tailed intervals.
An optimal interval is obtained for a single parameter in a discrete distribution under mean criteria.
Section 2 establishes uniform asymptotic size through behavior along qualitative drifting subsequences.
Explicit randomized mappings establish global asymptotic equivalence between positive Poisson and Gaussian experiments.

body.tldr: A staggered multiplicative panel with rare Poisson totals turns the Moreau--Kastler equation (3.14) proportional-effect setup into a discrete minimax confidence problem. The contribution derives the exact low-intensity deterministic value and all optimizers, proves a strict first-order gain from randomized interval kernels, prices the stronger all-untreated-zero fallback separately, and relates both procedures to the efficient high-intensity Gaussian limit. At every fixed algebraic observed design, failure probability and saved length are exponential--polynomial on target-membership strata; continuous extensions to the compact stratum closures reduce all extrema and one-sided limits to finitely many algebraically represented critical-component values, so strict rational comparisons terminate. The remaining open theorem asks for a uniform finite machine representation across shares and compact intensity ranges, including exact coverage contacts and the mandatory \(T=3\), \(\alpha=.05\), \(\kappa=.01\), \(K=2\), \(h=.01\) certificate with gap at most \(.05\).

project_justification.gap: Regular staggered-PPML work supplies the proportional target and high-information inference, while exact discrete interval work treats scalar families or finite-prior Monte Carlo approximations. Existing results do not convert fixed-design strict exponential--polynomial comparisons into a terminating rational-polyhedral cover that remains valid at nominal-coverage and target-endpoint contacts uniformly over observed shares and compact intensity ranges.
project_justification.niche: The nonregular object is the entire worst-nuisance expected-length frontier, with deterministic connected intervals, randomized kernels, and the all-untreated-zero restriction kept distinct under maintained aggregate-exposure boxes and calibrated known intensity.
project_justification.fill: The paper joins exact low-count values and a high-count efficiency bridge to a rigorous fixed-algebraic-design reduction: stratum-closure continuations capture attained extrema and unattained membership-switch limits through finitely many critical components. It also specifies a finite certificate format whose accepted rational data would prove global coverage, conservative upper risk, and an integrality-preserving lower bound with an explicit error ledger; existence and synthesis of that uniform certificate remain the stated open question.

body.related_work: Moreau-Kastler (2025), equation (3.14), supplies the imputed counterfactual-share proportional target; that algebraic specialization is setup rather than a novel theorem here. Wooldridge (2023) identifies staggered nonlinear cohort-time effects and makes pooled Poisson quasi-likelihood operational under fixed \(T\), while Martin (2017), Theorems 1--2, establishes regular fixed-\(T\) asymptotics for multiplicative-panel averages; both inform the high-information endpoint. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005), Theorem 1, supplies Bayes--minimax duality but does not calculate this multivariate connected-interval game. Kabaila and Byrne (2001) supply the ordered scalar exact-Poisson benchmark and the homogeneous known-mass reduction is only a sanity check. Kabaila (2013) supplies auxiliary-uniform atom splitting, and Habiger, McCann, and Tebbs (2013) studies integrated one-parameter discrete optimality. Bochnak, Coste, and Roy (1998) supply the classical semialgebraic projection, compatible-stratification, finite-component, and path facts used by the fixed-design reduction; the Poisson critical-equation cancellation and the treatment of discontinuous membership boundaries are derived here. Schafer and Stark (2009), especially Theorem 6 and the Conclusion, establish finite-prior Monte Carlo convergence and off-support risk control, but not a deterministic stopping rule, global continuum honesty, or a complete integer lower certificate. Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, characterize uniform asymptotic size through drifting subsequences, but do not provide finite rational cells, computable outward enclosures, or a terminating acceptance predicate. The open certificate question is stated as a strict finite verified strengthening of these last two guarantees. Brown, Carter, Low, and Zhang (2004), Theorems 1 and 3, informs the Poisson--Gaussian comparison without itself profiling this causal nuisance or transferring the connected-interval minimax game.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The fixed-design result does not claim that total coverage is one exponential--polynomial, that the discontinuous piecewise coverage function attains its extrema, or that equality contacts are decidable. It instead optimizes continuous fixed-profile extensions on compact stratum closures and includes unattained one-sided membership-switch limits; outward enclosures terminate only for strict rational comparisons. Uniformly parameterizing those contacts over the full observed-share simplex and compact intensity ranges remains open. The mandatory early-kill instance is \(T=3\), \(\alpha=.05\), \(\kappa=.01\), count box \(K=2\), and endpoint mesh \(.01\): it still requires an accepted globally share-uniform deterministic primal and a complete integer lower certificate with gap at most \(.05\). A nuisance grid, sampled-share check, fixed-share certificate, root linear-programming relaxation, or unbudgeted numerical gap does not pass.
body.honest_scope: The causal-functional identity is setup credited to Moreau-Kastler (2025), equation (3.14), and the homogeneous known-mass scalar reduction is a sanity check credited to Kabaila and Byrne (2001). The independent Poisson total law and share lower bound define the experiment; the exposure, time-effect, treatment-effect, and calibrated known-intensity restrictions are maintained rather than consequences of PPML theory. The fixed-algebraic-design separation result covers strict comparisons of closure-continuation extrema and one-sided limits, not exact equality contacts or a uniform finite cover. The latter remains an open-ended certificate question, including the early-kill construction. An unknown or estimated intensity changes the experiment and remains unsolved. No claim is made for noninteger outcomes, arbitrary overdispersion, individual-data sufficiency, or software-default intervals. The exact positive-intensity randomized value away from the low-count phase and the global closed-form maximizer of \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}\) are outside the promised theorem spine unless they emerge from the certificate analysis.
